title: Finite intersection limits in a finite ind-étale covering
statement: Let $X$ be affine, $U\in\mathcal B_X$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], and $\{V_a\to U\}_{a=1}^m$ a nonempty finite basis covering, indexed by $1\le a\le m$. There exist small nonempty directed sets $J_a$ and presentations $V_a=\varprojlim_{j_a\in J_a}V_{a,j_a}$ by affine étale finite-presentation $U$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra, def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Put $J=\prod_aJ_a$ with coordinatewise ordering. Every $\mathcal V_j=\{V_{a,j_a}\to U\}_a$ is an étale covering, with all members in $\mathcal B_X$. For every $p\ge0$ and ordered tuple $\alpha=(a_0,\ldots,a_p)$, including repetitions, set $T_\alpha=\prod_{r=0}^p{}_U V_{a_r}$ and $T_{\alpha,j}=\prod_{r=0}^p{}_U V_{a_r,j_{a_r}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. These are affine ind-étale over $X$, and $T_\alpha\cong\varprojlim_jT_{\alpha,j}$. All transitions are affine; the projections to stages and the limit identifications commute with every projection deleting a factor. No étaleness over $X$ is asserted for the first-limit stages.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$. By [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], $B$ and $C_a$ are ind-etale $A$-algebras. The $A$-algebra map $B\to C_a$ is ind-etale by the algebra-map clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Hence [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] presents $V_a$ as an inverse limit of affine etale finite-presentation $U$-schemes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to the filtered algebra diagram, or its opposite scheme diagram, to replace its index category by a nonempty directed set $J_a$ without changing its colimit or limit. All diagrams and directed replacements are small in the universe fixed by [def-weil-size-convention]. Denote the resulting projections by $q_{a,i}:V_a\to V_{a,i}$.

proof.text: The finite product $J=\prod_{a=1}^mJ_a$ is small and nonempty: choose one element in each factor. Given $j,k\in J$, choose an upper bound of $j_a,k_a$ in each $J_a$, giving an upper bound in $J$. The original basis covering is jointly surjective by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. For any $u\in U$, choose $v\in V_a$ mapping to $u$. Its image $q_{a,j_a}(v)\in V_{a,j_a}$ also maps to $u$. Thus every chosen stage family is jointly surjective, and its arrows are etale by construction; [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] makes it an etale covering. This uses no surjectivity of an individual limit projection.

proof.text: Each stage $V_{a,i}\to U$ is ind-etale, using its one-object etale presentation in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Compose with $U\to X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]; since $V_{a,i}$ is affine, [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] puts it in $\mathcal B_X$. Repeated application of the fibre-product clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] now puts both $T_\alpha$ and $T_{\alpha,j}$ in $\mathcal B_X$, including tuples with repetitions. Every transition in a factor system or an intersection system is a morphism between affine schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. This also makes the limit-to-stage projections affine.

source.place: Tag 099U (lemma-affine-vanishing), basis stability and the first-limit intersections

proof.text: Fix $a$. Reindex the cone for $V_a$ along $J\to J_a$. It is still a limit, as follows directly from the dual universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a compatible family $h_j:Z\to V_{a,j_a}$, the map at $j$ depends only on $j_a$: if $j_a=k_a=i$, take an upper bound $l\ge j,k$ with $l_a=i$; both maps equal $h_l$, since the transition at coordinate $a$ is the identity. Write this map as $h_i$. If $i\le i'$, choose $j\le k$ with $j_a=i$, $k_a=i'$ by holding the other coordinates fixed. Compatibility gives a cone $(h_i)$ over $J_a$, hence a unique map $Z\to V_a$. Conversely this map recovers every $h_j$. Thus $V_a=\varprojlim_{j\in J}V_{a,j_a}$ with exactly the original projections.

source.place: Tag 099U (lemma-affine-vanishing), product directed index set; explicit verification of coordinate reindexing

proof.text: For a tuple $\alpha=(a_0,\ldots,a_p)$, define $t_{\alpha,j}:T_\alpha\to T_{\alpha,j}$ by the maps $q_{a_r,j_{a_r}}$ on the respective factors. Existence, uniqueness and compatibility with transitions follow from the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. A cone $h_j:Z\to T_{\alpha,j}$ gives, by each factor projection, a cone $Z\to V_{a_r,j_{a_r}}$. Step 4 gives a unique map $h_r:Z\to V_{a_r}$. All $h_r$ have the same composite to $U$: at each stage this follows from the fibre product, and any two stage indices have a common upper bound. Therefore the $h_r$ give a unique map $h:Z\to T_\alpha$. Its composite with $t_{\alpha,j}$ is $h_j$, since they have equal projections to every factor. The same uniqueness proves that $h$ is the only such map. This is the limit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If $a_r=a_s$, the two factor cones and the maps $h_r,h_s$ remain separate; the argument never identifies them.

source.place: Tag 099U (lemma-affine-vanishing), displayed inverse-limit identity for all finite intersections; universal-property proof including repeated indices

proof.text: Let $d_r:T_\alpha\to T_{\alpha\setminus r}$ and $d_{r,j}:T_{\alpha,j}\to T_{\alpha\setminus r,j}$ delete the $r$th factor. Then $d_{r,j}t_{\alpha,j}=t_{\alpha\setminus r,j}d_r$: composing either side with any remaining factor projection gives $q_{a_s,j_{a_s}}\operatorname{pr}_s$ for $s\ne r$, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives equality. The same calculation proves commutation with every transition. Consequently the limit identifications in step 5 commute with deletion, by uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For deletion from a one-factor product take the empty product to be $U$; the equation is equality of the structure maps to $U$, and the constant $U$-diagram has limit $U$ since $J$ is nonempty and directed.
